gloss: to hire; to take on; to employ

definitions.gloss: to hire; to take on; to employ
definitions.explanation: To formally bring someone on as a worker or staff member. More deliberate and formal than plain {雇|やと}う, often used of a company taking on new personnel.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{社員|しゃいん}を{雇|やと}い{入|い}れる。
examples.english: We will take on a new employee.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{若|わか}い{人材|じんざい}を{雇|やと}い{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The company took on young talent.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{時期|じき}に{備|そな}えて、パートを{何人|なんにん}か{雇|やと}い{入|い}れることにした。
examples.english: We decided to take on several part-timers in preparation for the busy season.

notes:
Compound of {雇|やと}う (to employ) + {入|い}れる (to take in). The {入|い}れる element stresses bringing the person into the organization, so it suits formal hiring of staff.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社員|しゃいん}を{雇|やと}い{入|い}れる: to take on an employee
- {人材|じんざい}を{雇|やと}い{入|い}れる: to bring on talent
- {新|あら}たに{雇|やと}い{入|い}れる: to newly hire

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {雇|やと}う: to employ; to hire — the plain, everyday verb; {雇|やと}い{入|い}れる sounds more formal and organizational
